World.title: FIFA World Cup: FIVE teams eliminated, ONE from Africa
World.content:
Can Bafana Bafana claim an unlikely place in the last 32? Photo: ESPN FC

The FIFA World Cup is starting to take shape. However, five nations are officially heading home. Bafana Bafana are still in the hunt for a spot in the last 32.

Bafana are still in the running at the FIFA World Cup 2026

South Africa’s matchday 2 draw against the Czech Republic leaves them with a fighting chance of progressing to the knockout phase of the 2026 World Cup. Things started disastrously for Bafana, with a 2-0 defeat against Mexico, which saw Hugo Broos’ men finish the match with nine players. A rather large spanner in the works for Broos is how to line up his midfield unit without midfield maestro Teboho Mokoena. The Sundowns man is unavailable for the clash against the Republic of Korea after an accumulation of bookings. Bafana vs Korea kicks off at 03:00 in the wee hours of Thursday morning. Set your alarms, or drink a lot of coffee. Five nations are officially heading home. They are the gallant Haiti, North Africans Tunisia, Jordan, Panama and a talented yet under-achieving Turkiye side.

All you need to know about the Bafana squad

19 of the 26-man squad named by Hugo Broos play in the Betway Premiership.



Ex-Orlando Pirates star Lyle Foster is the only British-based player, recently relegated from the Premier League with Burnley.

Uncapped 22-year-old defender Olwethu Makhanya is on the books of United States MLS side Philadelphia Union. The squad contains eight players from the newly crowned champions, Orlando Pirates. Mamelodi Sundowns, champions in eight of the last nine PSL campaigns, also have eight representatives

World.title: 6 ways the iCaur 03T iWD is just like your iPhone
World.content:
Here it is, the iCaur 03T iWD. And based on the amount of attention it gets, South Africans are besotted with it. Which is ironic, because it wasn’t supposed to be called that at all. Chery’s all-electric sub-brand is supposed to be ‘iCar’ and so it is in mainland China. However, everywhere else in the world, the marque bolted on a ‘u’ for good measure to avoid any lawsuits …

Funny story, Apple still owns the rights to ‘iCar.’ Not because Apple ever sold one. But because it spent the better part of a decade and several billion dollars trying to build a self-driving electric car. Eventually, it euthanised the whole project and shelved the name like a trophy nobody’s allowed to touch. Turns out building cars is hard. But Chery knuckled down and got on with producing the car Apple never could … Meow!

ICAUR 03T IWD

You’ll note an almost total absence of badging on the vehicle, except for the light signatures themselves. Image: Ray Leathern

Nevertheless, the R699 900 iCaur 03T iWD feels less like irony and more like prophecy after spending a decent amount of seat time in it. Do so, and it quickly becomes apparent that iCaur didn’t just draw inspiration from Apple, but it pays homage in its entire brand philosophy. As we shall now explain …



1. FLAT AND FLUSH

Apple spent twenty years convincing people that a seamless slab of aluminium is inherently superior to anything with visible screws. The iCaur 03T iWD pulls off the same trick with its all-aluminium underpinnings, flat edges and door handles that sit flush against the bodywork. Until you unlock it that is, at which point they motor outward like the car is greeting you. It’s pure theatre, and it makes it look like you’ve bought something much more expensive than it really is. Approve!

2. TOUCHSCREEN-TASTIC

There are a few Chinese oddities in here but, in the main, its minimalist approach aligns with Apple-type philosophies. Image: Ray Leathern

Just like the iPhone, the iCaur 03T iWD only really comes alive once you tap the 15.4-inch touchscreen. Of course, it runs wireless Apple CarPlay seamlessly, which means the rest of the user interface is pretty much ignored. Chery built the car, but Apple still owns the user experience (UX). Like many of the other Chinese cars we’ve driven recently, the high-definition graphics are similar. But fit, finish and noise dampening is feels a cut above here.

3. ICAUR 03T IWD UPSELL

The test unit you see before you is the ‘Allroad’ or iWD. Same shell, same screen, same chunky 19-inch alloys in each corner. But here you get a second motor on the real axle for superb traction. The iCaur 03T iWD jumps from 135 kW to 205 kW and 385 Nm of torque. Zero to 100 km/h zips by in 6.5 seconds. The performance is breathtaking and maintaining your spot in traffic is a cinch with its instant throttle response and tall driving position. It’s just like that upgrade from the 128 GB to the 256 GB iPhone. Unmistakable Tim Cook.

4. ACCESSORISE, ACCESSORISE

Pushing the wheels out as far as possible to each corner of the chassis doesn’t just do wonders for the proportions, it enhances the handling, too. Image: Ray Leathern

Another parallel is the accessory ecosystem you didn’t ask for but will probably buy and enjoy anyway. The iCaur 03T iWD has a chunky side-opening tailgate, which is brilliant for a bit of extra privacy when changing after a run/bike/surf. It also hides a rectangular storage box adding 40 litres of space for dirty/wet items you don’t want inside the vehicle. This is iCaur’s answer to AirPods perhaps. A 12-speaker Infinity sound system is justifiably premium tier, too. Something your ears will notice, even if your wallet doesn’t.

5. IT’S ALL IMAGE

Next is what the iCaur 03T iWD signals about you as the driver. In our eyes, most electric vehicles (EVs) announce that you’re a bit in the blue-bubble club. However, turning up in total silence in this R699 900 future retro off-roader announces something else entirely – that you’re supercool. It’s basically badge-less, with zero identifying features … and that makes people go gaga over it. Ironic isn’t it, that in this day and age of information overload, withholding obvious identifying characteristics is the one way to really get noticed!

6. BATTERY LIFE

Finally, here’s the bit both brands would rather we didn’t talk about – real-world battery life. Every iPhone owner knows the feeling of watching their battery percentage evaporate in real time. To the iCaur 03T iWD’s credit, it’s not overly optimistic. The claim on the NEDC rating is 436 km from its 69-kWh battery pack. At the same time, it starts each charge with an ambitious 500 km on the display. However, over a week of urban-only driving, the most we completed was 330 km on a single charge. Yes, this was in Eco mode exclusively with air conditioning for comfort. Could we have hypermiled it further? Possibly, but driving like that also precludes you from the instant-throttle joy of an EV.



ICAUR 03T IWD VERDICT

Side-hinged rear door is supercool, much like everything else on this baby off-road EV. Image: Ray Leathern

At the end of the day – range anxiety or no – we absolutely adored the iCaur 03T iWD. We didn’t know what to expect from this mini electric G-Wagon wannabe … but we enjoyed every moment of it. It’s that rarest of things, an EV with character. As proven by passersby who couldn’t help themselves staring open-mouthed, trying to figure out what it is. Apple may have killed off its car a long time ago, but Chery went and built its vision anyway. And all it asks for the pleasure of driving it is a miserly R699 900! You don’t even need to work for the new lottery operator to afford that …

But what do you think? Will South Africans finally warm to EVs thanks to this fun little battery-powered off roader? Share your thoughts in the comments section below …

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs news: Da Cruz truth bombs, THREE new signings?
World.content:
Today’s Kaizer Chiefs news wrap takes a closer look at new coach Fernando Da Cruz. There are also several names being linked to the club.

Meet the new Kaizer Chiefs boss

As you’ll know by now, Kaizer Chiefs have hired a new manager. There will be pressure on 53-year-old Frenchman Fernando Da Cruz to instil a proper playing identity at one of African football’s truly massive clubs. Because he’s known for his emphasis on tactical discipline and defensive structure, Chiefs fans shouldn’t be expecting their team to go all guns blazing to win games by halftime. After several periods of upheaval and interim managerial stints, fans will be eager to see the club stick with one man for an extended period. He’s also got an interesting background, too.

A student of Marcelo Bielsa

Da Cruz worked alongside the legendary Argentine Marcelo Bielsa at Lille. Da Cruz had three stints with the French outfit in several roles. Namely, as a scout, caretaker manager and head coach of the B side, where he nurtured talents such as Idrissa Gueye, Lucas Digne, Victor Osimhen, and Eden Hazard. This will be music to the ears of Chiefs fans. They always champion the youth players who come through the club’s structures.

Rumoured Kaizer Chiefs targets

According to Eliot Mahlase, Chiefs should be gunning for a new striker to partner Flavio Silva. Junior Dion, Tshegofatso Mabasa and Pirates’ talented midfielder Kabelo Dlamini are his picks.

World.title: He’s BACK! Leon Schuster releases new World Cup song [video]
World.content:
Leon Schuster has released another rugby anthem. Images via YouTube screenshot

After taking a hiatus due to poor health, popular comedian and TV actor Leon Schuster has returned to the spotlight with a new song in time for the Rugby World Cup. The 75-year-old’s latest offering is dedicated to Springboks coach Rassie Erasmus.

It comes after Schuster suffered a in recent years that have limited his mobility and left him with chronic pain. He has also spoken out about living with depression and loneliness.

LEON SCHUSTER IS BACK WITH AN ODE TO RASSIE

Over the weekend, Leon Schuster released the music video to his new single titled Miljoene Hande vir Rassie.

The Rugby World Cup song is dedicated to Springboks coach Rassie Erasmus.



The video is heavily influenced by AI visuals, featuring scenes of rugby fans in a stadium cheering on the Springboks, Schuster and Rassie enjoying a beer and a braai and the “Bomb Squad” gearing up for action.

“Rassie die koning van die Bomb Squad [Rassie is the king of the Bomb Squad” Leon sings in one scene.

Schuster – who has also been behind rugby anthems Hier Kom Die Bokke and Bokmasjien – hopes to honour Rassie with the song.



He said, “Rassie is the lion of the rugby jungle. He doesn’t get pursued; he pursues with his unorthodox methods and his will to persevere. That is my man, Rassie.”

‘HIGH SPIRITS’ AMID HEALTH SETBACK

In recent years, Leon Schuster has suffered from chronic back pain and limited mobility due to severe injury sustained on a film set.

The star, known for his films like You Must Be Joking, Oh Schucks, I’m Gatvol, and Mr Bones, among many others, has undergone four surgeries and bedridden recoveries. 

Now he is slowly claiming back his life, remaining in “high spirits”,

He recently celebrated Father’s Day and his 75th birthday surrounded by loved ones.

World.title: ‘The Polygamist’: Link between hit Netflix show and Jacob Zuma
World.content:
South African Netflix series The Polygamist has taken the world by storm for its captivating storyline about serial cheater Jonasi Gomora and his multiple wives and children. The production is based on the book by Zimbabwean author Sue Nyathi and is produced, amongst others, by Thuli Nomaqhawe Zuma and Gugu Zuma Ncube, the daughters of former president Jacob Zuma.

Like Gomora, Zuma is also a well-known polygamist.

THE POLYGAMIST PRODUCED BY JACOB ZUMA’S DAUGHTER

Over the past few days, The Polygamist has gained worldwide traction, garnering millions of views and landing on the most-viewed lists in over a dozen countries.

As the name suggests, the 22-episode series is based on polygamy – between hot-shot businessman Jonasi Gomora, played by actor Sdumo Mtshali – and his multiple wives, Joyce, Essie, Matipa and his young lover, Lindani. 

It is also centred on real-life issues like domestic violence, infidelity, toxic masculinity, casual hook-ups, sexually-transmitted diseases and generational trauma.

It is based on the book, The Polygamist, written by Zimbabwean author Sue Nyathi, and is produced by Gugu Zuma Ncube and Thuli Nomaqhawe Zuma.

Coincidentally, Thuli and Gugu’s father, former President Jacob Zuma, is a well-known polygamist.



The link hasn’t gone unnoticed by viewers.

TikToker Thando B Khumalo posted: “I find it interesting that The Polygamist was produced by the daughter of the country’s most famous polygamist”.

Others speculated whether the siblings were related to the storyline.



Zuma is reported to have six legally recognised wives and multiple children.

WHO IS JONASI GOMORA BASED ON?

Despite the speculation, The Polygamist is “a work of fiction” and not based on a true story, says author Sue Nyathi.

She told The Herald: “I have come to realise that he is a narcissist. And I didn’t see him that way when I wrote the story. It’s only now that I understand that’s what he is — his character embodies that. He is not based on anyone.



“The fact that so many people can point to Jonasi is a testament to the strength of the characterisation. It cannot be a single person. People are now saying, ‘My father, brother or husband is a Jonasi,’ so it clearly cannot be one individual. The series is popular because people can relate to the characters”.

‘POLYGAMY IS MY CULTURE’

Like The Polygamist lead character Jonasi Gomora, Jacob Zuma has defended polygamy as being part of his African identity.



He told Newsweek in 2010: “That’s my culture. It does not take anything from me, from my political beliefs and everything, including the belief in the equality of women.

He added: “The problem is that when people have their own culture, they think [it] is the only right one. The only one accepted by God.

“People interpret cultures in different ways. Some think that their culture is superior to others; that’s a problem we have in the world.”

World.title: Emergency power outage to hit 16 Johannesburg areas TOMORROW
World.content:
The emergency power outage will occur for two hours at Brynorth Substation. PHOTO: Pexels

An emergency power outage will affect 16 Johannesburg areas at Brynorth Substation on Wednesday, 24 June 2026, according to a statement by City Power Johannesburg.

The outage will occur in the morning from 9:00 to 11:00, lasting for two hours.

It is caused by essential maintenance work that needs to be done on their electricity network to ensure good service provision.



EMERGENCY OUTAGE AFFECTS 16 AREAS

Here is a list of areas that the outage will affect, according to City Power Johannesburg:

Post Office

Ebury Road

Eileen Road

Logan Road

Hobart Road

Portman Road

Norman Distributor

Muswell Distributor

Elgin Drive

Struben Road

Eaton Avenue

Knights Bridge

Baker Distributor

William Nicol Road

Epsom Downs Checkers

Main Road (Bryanston Drive)

City Power Johannesburg, an electricity power utility, cautioned customers to treat their electricity supply points as live.

THREE PROPERTIES INSPECTED IN JOHANNESBURG ILLEGAL CONNECTIONS CRACKDOWN

Three properties were inspected in Johannesburg on Tuesday, 23 June 2026, as part of a citywide operation targeting illegal electricity connections. The Mayoral High Impact Service Delivery initiative is currently conducting the operation across the city to disconnect properties found with illegal connections, according to an X post by City Power Johannesburg.

The first property, on Northumberland Street in South Kensington, was found with a bypassed electricity meter. It also had an open circuit connected to the meter, indicating possible tampering and non-compliance with municipal regulations. The property received a level one disconnection, a disconnection whereby electricity is switched off in a lockable distribution box.

The second property is located on Galteemore Street in Kensington. The site consists of an open space where a kitchen and car wash are being operated. An inspection was conducted to locate the electricity meter; however, no meter was found on the premises, suggesting the property may be drawing power without a registered connection.

The third property inspected was located in a different area on Idah Street in Cyrildene. The property is a residential premise used for dwelling purposes. After a thorough inspection, no irregularities, tampering, or non-compliance issues were identified. The property was fully compliant.

World.title: Red or green? For Brazil, the politics of World Cup kits matter
World.content:
BRASILIA - When Brazil faces Scotland in the World Cup on Wednesday, the South American team's goalkeeper Alisson Becker will be dressed in a green kit -- not the red one originally approved by FIFA.

In any other country, such a wardrobe change might have gone unnoticed, but not in Brazil where the national team's colours have become the subject of a deep political dispute.

The Selecao's iconic yellow and green jerseys were co-opted years ago by conservatives aligned with far-right former president Jair Bolsonaro -- who is serving time for plotting a coup after losing the 2022 elections to Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva.

And while Lula has set out to reclaim the colours of Brazil's flag in his push to reelection in October, red -- not typically part of Team Brazil's gear -- is the colour of the left and his party.

World.title: AC sales soar as Europe wilts under record heat
World.content:
PARIS - Europe braced for another day of an unprecedented heatwave that has smashed records in many countries and sent air conditioner sales zooming in a continent unused and ill-equipped to handle searing heat.

The extreme weather is being driven by atmospheric and circulation patterns that keep hot air trapped in place for days, causing the mercury to slowly rise, with these factors exacerbated by global warming, experts say.

France's national temperature indicator -- an average of daytime and nighttime temperatures across 30 stations -- reached 29.8C on Tuesday, the hottest since measurements began in 1947.

Sales of fans and air conditioners, meanwhile, skyrocketed in a country where most buildings are not designed to deal with extreme heat.

On Monday, hypermarket operator Carrefour had sold 30,000 units by 6:30 pm – "a thousand times more than on a normal day", CEO Alexandre Bompard said.

Sales on Amazon nearly doubled last week compared with the same period in 2025, whilst electronics outlet Fnac Darty reported double-digit growth.

Thierry, an electrician in south-west France, said he was overwhelmed by requests for "emergency" air-conditioning installations.

"In theory, you have to submit a request to the owners' association general meeting" in residential complexes "but people don't want to wait."

"It's difficult to live" alone and without air conditioning, said Martine Belloc, a 62-year-old retiree in Bordeaux, who on Tuesday went to La ManuCo, a coworking site that mobilised to welcome elderly people.

With four more French departments being put under the highest heat alert category Wednesday, some 44 million people are affected, according to AFP calculations.

Added to the 31 departments currently on orange alert, more than 90 percent of the French population is exposed to extreme heat, with temperatures of 39C to 41C expected on Wednesday from Brittany to the Paris region, and in much of the south-west.

World.title: England left frustrated by Ghana in World Cup draw
World.content:
BOSTON - England suffered a World Cup setback on Tuesday as Thomas Tuchel's side were held to a frustrating 0-0 draw by Ghana, leaving them with work still do as they bid to progress to the knockout stage as Group L winners.

Nico O'Reilly came closest to scoring for England with a late header that hit the bar and captain Harry Kane blasted the rebound over the woodwork, but after the promise of their opening 4-2 win over Croatia, this was a performance that will raise doubts about their chances of winning the tournament.

England dominated possession and had 19 shots to their opponents' two, yet rarely looked like scoring past Ghana's stand-in goalkeeper Benjamin Asare in a match watched by 63,983 fans at the Gillette Stadium near Boston.

Both teams have four points with one group game still to play, with progression to the next round all but assured but their final positions still in the balance.

Kane admitted he had hoped for a better result.

"Obviously disappointed not to win the game," he told the BBC. "It's a game we could've walked away 1-0, 2-0 and moved on. It was never going to be the prettiest game because of the way they played.

"Credit to them, they defended well, dangerous on the counter-attack... We take the point and move on."

In damp, cool conditions, England delivered a stodgy performance that echoed some of their faltering displays during Euro 2024.

However, there are no dramatic consequences, as they take a step closer to the last 32. All they need do now is safely negotiate their final group fixture against Panama at the MetLife Stadium on Saturday, and they can turn their attentions to the knockout rounds.

England have still never lost to African opposition at the World Cup, and that record was rarely at risk of ending here.

Ghana nevertheless battled brilliantly, as the nation ranked 73rd in the world -- 69 places behind England -- put up a determined display.

- Partey plays, Kane quiet -

The late decision by the Black Stars to appoint Carlos Queiroz as coach is looking increasingly justified, with this result following their opening 1-0 win over Panama. The 2010 quarter-finalists face Croatia next in Philadelphia.

Thomas Partey returned for Ghana after missing the Panama match in Toronto because Canadian authorities denied him a visa -- the ex-Arsenal midfielder is facing trial on rape charges in the UK.

Asare of local side Hearts of Oak started in goal for the Ghanaians after coming on for the injured Lawrence Ati Zigi against Panama.

England's inability to regularly test him will be a source of concern, as Kane was kept quiet and failed to add to his 10 World Cup goals -- he remains level with Gary Lineker as their all-time top scorer at the tournament.

Noni Madueke and Anthony Gordon were unable to make the difference on the wings and their substitutes could not have a decisive impact this time.

Jude Bellingham won his 50th cap as Marc Guehi and Djed Spence replaced John Stones and O'Reilly in the defence.

A Declan Rice free-kick that sailed just over was about as close as England came in the opening half. In fact it took almost an hour for Asare to make a notable save, but it was a comfortable one to deny Gordon.

Ghana may feel Jordan Pickford should have been punished for charging out of his box and crashing into Prince Adu without touching the ball -- but instead the goalkeeper was given a free-kick.

There was also panic for England when substitute Adu ran through into the area but could not get a shot away.

Then the pressure was turned up a notch in the closing minutes, as Asare denied Bukayo Saka with a good stop low to his left before O'Reilly headed off the woodwork from close range and Kane blazed over.

World.title: US TV news host begs for info after kidnap note says mother is dead
World.content:
LOS ANGELES - A popular US television news host whose mother was kidnapped in February said she is in "agony" after reports the elderly woman died shortly after being abducted.

Savannah Guthrie, the anchor of a major morning network news program, pleaded for anyone with information about the disappearance of Nancy Guthrie, 84, to contact authorities.

"I wanted to just take the opportunity to ask people, to really... to beg people to come forward, somebody knows something," she told viewers of NBC's "Today" show.

"This is a news story today that is on your radar, but this is the life that my sister lives, that I live, that my brother lives, that our extended families live, that our children live every day, and we are in agony, we cannot be at peace.

"This is a moment to tell you that we need your help."

Guthrie's emotional appeal came after US media reported that one of two apparently credible notes sent to the family in the weeks after Guthrie was kidnapped indicated she was dead.

The first note had demanded millions of dollars in Bitcoin for her safe return, while the second said that she had died.

CNN reported the note indicated the kidnappers had not intended to kill her.

The February 1 kidnapping in Tucson, Arizona made headlines in the United States.

Interest intensified when security camera footage released by authorities showed a masked, apparently armed man at the house, which lies in the desert suburbs of the city.

Amateur sleuths have descended on the area and much ink has been spilled on the case.

US President Donald Trump said Tuesday he had been following the case.

"I hope they find her," he told reporters. "That family has gone through hell."

Savannah Guthrie has previously offered $1 million for a tip leading to the recovery of her mother, while the FBI has offered $100,000 for information.

"We're begging for your help," she told viewers again on Tuesday, shortly before a tipline number was displayed on screen.

"Please, if you're watching, no matter how small... the reward is there. You can tell us, it can be anonymous," she said.

"Please do the right thing for us, for our family, for our children, and we love our mom, and we'll never stop looking for her, never."

The "Today" show is a US institution, airing nationally since 1952 and drawing millions of viewers to NBC on weekday mornings.

World.title: Youngsters pushing experienced Boks
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - A new generation of Springboks is bringing fresh energy to the national setup.

Their enthusiasm has been impossible to ignore, pushing standards higher and challenging established stars.

Captain Siya Kolisi says the youngsters have been a welcome addition to the squad. And it's yet another reminder of the talent pipeline driving South African rugby forward.

"The energy they bring to the team is really amazing," Kolisi said.

"When we were training with the under 20s group the intensity was really high because they are fearless and they don't know what the limit is. It was really good for us as a team. It's really been exciting and going well."

World.title: 'Can't afford repeat of July 2021': Cachalia warns against criminality
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - Acting Police Minister Firoz Cachalia says police are ready to keep the country safe on 30 June.

He was speaking during a media briefing on Tuesday in Cape Town, where he outlined the preparedness ahead of the deadline.

This comes amid calls by anti-illegal immigration groups demanding the removal of undocumented foreign nationals by month-end.

"The right to protest shouldn't be used as an excuse for criminality and abusive behaviour," Cachalia said.

"Only the police and other officials have the responsibility to enforce the law in a constitutional democracy. We cannot afford a repeat of what happened on July 2021. And in this case, we also have situations where people are making inflammatory statements on social media, statements that they are going to expel people from our country themselves on the 30th. And we see that kind of behaviour already. It's a minority phenomenon."

Cachalia said the Western Cape has had about 30 marches, six which were accompanied by violence.

"The minister of police can't take the posture which says, well, whatever happens on the 30th is acceptable. My responsibility is to make sure that our people and the resources of the police is mobilised to keep the country safe."

Cachalia said while the army has not been deployed, the the need to call up the troops will arise in an instance where their services are needed to protect critical infrastructure
